name: Privileged Access Inventory and Elevation Record
description: The population of identities holding administrative or production-data privilege, together with the record of privilege elevations across the period showing who elevated, when, why, and for how long.

expected_content.element: Complete list of identities holding privileged entitlements, with the entitlement named
expected_content.why: Establishes the standing-privilege population, which is what least privilege is assessed against.

expected_content.element: Distinction between standing privilege and privilege held only through elevation
expected_content.why: These carry very different risk and are frequently conflated in a single export.

expected_content.element: Elevation events with actor, timestamp, duration, and target system
expected_content.why: Demonstrates that just-in-time privilege actually expires rather than being nominally temporary.
Elevation records without justification evidence that elevation happened, not that it was appropriate.

expected_content.element: Identification of non-human identities holding privilege
expected_content.why: Service accounts frequently hold the broadest privilege and are the most common omission.

expected_content.element: Segregation-of-duties conflicts present in the population
expected_content.why: Supports the conflict-detection element of the control where one is claimed.

owner: IT / Identity and Access Management owner
source_system_examples: Privileged access management platform session and elevation log
Cloud provider IAM policy analysis export

freshness_expectation.rationale: DriftGuard default for a continuously operating control. Not an audit rule.

redaction_guidance: Never include session recordings, command transcripts, or credential material.
Retain identity attribution; the artifact has no value without it.
retention_guidance: Retain elevation records for the full examination period; retention shorter than the period leaves an untestable interval.

validation_rules.rule: A privileged access inventory exists for each in-scope system.
The inventory includes non-human identities and reconciles to the identity provider population.
Elevation records carry a justification and a bounded duration.
Elevation records span the full examination period.
The systems covered fall within the declared system boundary.
The export originates from the platform enforcing elevation, not from a maintained register.

common_issues.issue: Elevation is nominally time-bounded but sessions are renewed indefinitely.
common_issues.impact: Standing privilege in effect, with the appearance of just-in-time control.

common_issues.issue: Service accounts with broad privilege excluded from the inventory as out of scope.
Break-glass accounts present with no record of whether they were used.
common_issues.impact: Cannot distinguish an unused emergency path from routine privileged access.

source_refs.supports: Expected content, persuasiveness weighting, and the common issues list.
Freshness window, sensitivity classification, and redaction guidance.

notes: Where an entity operates standing privilege deliberately, this artifact still applies: the inventory is the evidence, and elevation records are simply absent. That is not a deficiency by itself.
